name: Regenerate & Relink – Thumbnails, Image URLs & Media Cleanup
author: Takashi Fujisaki

sections.description:
WordPress bakes image size file names into your post content the moment you insert an image. When a size definition changes later — a new theme, new media settings — regenerating thumbnails is not enough: the URLs in your content still point to the old files, leaving broken images or outdated dimensions. Unused thumbnails pile up and waste disk space.

Regenerate & Relink fixes the whole chain, safely:

  • Diagnose – list every registered image size with file counts, disk usage, how often it is used in content, and which files need regeneration.
  • Regenerate – rebuild intermediate sizes from the original images. Never from -scaled copies.
  • Relink – update image URLs, width / height attributes and [caption] widths in post content to match the current definitions. Only the file name part of the URL is touched — your CDN and site structure are preserved.
  • Clean up – quarantine files that are no longer referenced anywhere, instead of deleting them. Restore anytime; auto-purge after 30 days (configurable).
  • Dry-run first – every stage shows a full preview before touching anything. Skipped items are reported with reasons and links.
  • WP-CLI – scan, review reports and apply from the command line.

The plugin never changes your image size definitions. It detects what was changed elsewhere — Settings > Media, your theme's add_image_size() — and brings files and content back in sync.
